content.thinking: I'm drafting the postmortem, clarifying that the impact was elevated latency rather than error rate, and flagging key assumptions—the causal link to the deploy is based on timing correlation rather than verified evidence, recovery is attributed to the rollback based only on latency metrics returning to baseline, and the ClientDisconnected errors predate the incident at the same rate, so tying them to the latency issue is an assumption rather than a confirmed fact. Now I'm moving into writing the executive summary.

assumptions: The deploy was linked to the slowdown by timing correlation (the latency rise began in the same minute as the release) plus the nature of the code change; no profiling or request-level tracing was done to prove the O(n^2) loop was the bottleneck.
Recovery is attributed to the rollback because latency returned to baseline shortly after it was applied; no separate test was run to rule out the slowdown subsiding on its own.

The ClientDisconnected errors in the logs were interpreted as shoppers abandoning slow page loads. These errors were present at a similar rate before the onset, so they are not clear evidence of incident impact on their own.
The alert fired roughly five minutes after the onset, so the first minutes of the slowdown were reconstructed from metrics and logs rather than observed live.
Impact on shoppers is inferred from server-side latency and log lines only; there is no client-side or business-metric data on how many people actually abandoned a page or a purchase.
input.executive_summary: For about six minutes early on 28 September 2026, the account page of the online shop became very slow to load. Shoppers could still use the site and almost all requests still succeeded — the error rate stayed at its normal everyday level and did not rise above it — but pages that normally returned in a fraction of a second took several seconds, and a small number of shoppers gave up and closed their browsers before the page finished loading. The cause was a code change released minutes earlier that made the page do far more work than necessary each time it was viewed. Automated monitoring raised an alert, the recent release was identified as the likely cause, and the release was rolled back; page load times returned to normal immediately afterwards. A draft code fix has been opened for review so the change can be corrected and re-released safely. No data was lost and no other part of the shop was affected.
input.root_cause: A deploy of io-shop at 07:03:00Z (revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655) changed `average_spend_per_item` to recompute an account's running total from scratch on every purchase — an O(n^2) loop — instead of reusing the account's carried total, making the account-page render path dramatically slower per request. Latency percentiles jumped in the same minute as the deploy (p50, p95 and p99 all rose roughly five- to tenfold), and rolling the service back off that revision returned latency to baseline.
